title: prune-sparse-controlplane-columns-and-add-read-path-telemetry
creator: Samir Patel
body:
Summary:
We will remove low-value / sparsely populated columns across the control-plane primary tables (projects, tenants, allocations, usage_events) and replace heavy join patterns with tenant-scoped read materializations and read-path telemetry. Goal is to reduce average row width by ~30%, cut cold-scan CPU during tenant listing queries, and provide per-query telemetry to catch regressions post-migration.

Why now:
- Disk usage and hot-scan CPU have steadily increased; several large customers hit tail-latency spikes during tenant list and billing snapshot queries.
- Previous partial fixes reduced index bloat but schema drift keeps reintroducing sparse fields.
- Cleaning schema and adding telemetry gives us measurable signals for regressions and a safer rollout path.

Scope and non-goals:
- In scope: identify sparse columns (NULL > 95% or very low cardinality) in core control-plane tables, add migration scripts to drop or move those columns into an archive table, create tenant-scoped materialized read views (updated via scheduled incremental refresh), implement lightweight per-query read_path telemetry (duration, rows_examined, indexes_used).
- Out of scope: deep normalization of all JSON blobs (separate ticket), redesign of public API surface, and client-side SDK changes.

Key decisions and trade-offs:
- Approach: Online copy-and-swap for each table instead of immediate ALTER DROP to avoid long locks. This uses staged shadow tables and batched backfills. Trade-off: longer migration window vs near-zero downtime.
- Materialized views vs caching layer: chose materialized views refreshed incrementally because it is simpler operationally and gives DB-native consistency for audit/billing queries.
- Telemetry: implement built-in query tags and an internal telemetry table (small, append-only) rather than external tracing, to keep telemetry queryable from the control plane without high sampling costs.

Success criteria:
- Production queries that previously scanned wide rows see median CPU time reduction >= 25% and P99 latency reduction >= 30% for tenant list and billing snapshot routes within 2 weeks of rollout.
- Overall primary table row width reduction >= 20% after all migrations.
- No user-facing downtime or failed canary tenants during rollout.
- Telemetry shows <1% of queries with missing indexes used post-migration; any regression triggers automatic alerting.

Estimated risk and mitigation:
- Risk: Backfill stalls due to large historical tables. Mitigation: batched backfills with resumable cursors and a kill-switch to revert to old table.
- Risk: Incorrect FK assumptions on archived columns. Mitigation: validate referential integrity with dry-run checks before swap; keep archived columns for 30 days before purge.

Milestones:
1) 2025-01-20: Column discovery run and candidate list (completed).
2) 2025-01-27: Migration tooling (shadow table pattern + resumable backfill) ready in staging.
3) 2025-02-03: Telemetry schema + query-tagging implemented and deployed to staging.
4) 2025-02-10: Canary migrations for low-traffic tenant subset.
5) 2025-02-24: Full rollout window (throttled).
6) 2025-03-14: Post-mortem and final purge of archived columns (if metrics green).
acceptance_criteria: migration scripts run via CI and pass dry-run checks
canary on 5 production tenants with no errors for 48h
observability dashboards display pre/post metrics and show >=25% CPU reduction on target queries
archived columns retained for minimum 30 days before purge
migration_plan: Plan: For each table (projects, tenants, allocations, usage_events) we will: 1) create shadow table with target schema (dropped sparse columns moved to archived_columns JSONB). 2) backfill in batches with a resumable cursor using primary key ranges and chunk-size throttling. 3) reconcile FK/unique constraints via staged verification queries. 4) create triggers for real-time delta capture during backfill window. 5) when backfill lag < 500ms for canary tenants, perform swap under brief lock and release triggers. 6) monitor telemetry and query dashboards for 72h before scheduling next table. Tools: internal migrator (git ref control-plane/migrator@v2.3), pg_repack for intermediate index cleanup, psql scripts for verification.
rollback_plan: If any canary shows increased error rates or latency regressions >10% at P95: 1) Pause further migrations. 2) Re-enable old table name (we retain pre-swap copy) by swapping back and disabling new triggers. 3) Run quick integrity checks to validate swap reversal. 4) Post-mortem and fix migration scripts (root cause) before resuming. Full purge of archived columns is gated behind 30-day safety window.
testing_notes: staging run with synthetic 10x traffic completed (2025-01-30)
integration tests include FK validation and delta trigger verification
load tests show backfill concurrency of 4 batches without exceeding 60% CPU on DB-primary
comments: 2025-01-20 - Samir Patel: Initial discovery run completed. Found ~14 candidate columns across 4 tables with NULL > 96% or very low cardinality. Added candidates list to drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/CONTROLPLANE-SCHEMA
2025-01-23 - Claire Nguyen: Reviewed migration pattern. Agreed to use shadow table + trigger delta approach. Action: create migration playbook and add to runbook library.
2025-01-28 - Diego Martinez: PR opened for migrator updates: https://github.com/redwood-inference/control-plane/pull/982 (includes resumable cursor logic). Requesting review from infra team.
2025-02-01 - Ops Team (infra-oncall): Deployed query tagging to staging. Telemetry table schema: query_tag, duration_ms, rows_examined, tenant_id, indexes_hint. Hooked into existing alerting.
2025-02-02 - Claire Nguyen: Canary schedule approved for 2025-02-10 across tenants t-101, t-314, t-271. Monitoring playbook assigned to @oncall-db and @sre.

2025-02-02 - Samir Patel: Note about cleanup window: archived_columns JSONB will be populated with dropped fields and retained for 30 days. After purge, we will run ANALYZE/REINDEX on affected tables.
